title: Evolution of electron spin resonance through a metallic quantum critical phase diagram
authors: Marc Scheffler, Jörg Sichelschmidt, Conrad Clauss, Mojtaba Javaheri Rahim, Boris I. Kochelaev, Cornelius Krellner, Christoph Geibel, Frank Steglich, Martin Dressel
abstract: In the heavy-fermion metal YbRh2Si2, quantum criticality at a suppressed antiferromagnetic order is governed by the interplay of local magnetic moments and itinerant conduction electrons. We demonstrate how this can be investigated by a new experimental approach that enables the observation of electron spin resonance (ESR) across a broad range of frequencies and fields at very low temperatures. This allowed us to cover a large part of the phase diagram from the paramagnetic Fermi-liquid phase to the phase with antiferromagnetic order and including the quantum-critical regime. Both the ESR g-factor and the linewidth present distinct behaviors in these three regimes, providing further insight into the physics across a quantum critical point. Notably, when cooling down at a field directly towards the quantum critical point, both g-factor and linewidth continuously decrease. Furthermore, we observe a very good matching of the g-factor behavior upon field-tuning and temperature-tuning towards the quantum-critical point. We analyze and discuss the results in the context of present theories on ESR in strongly correlated electron systems.
summary: This work uses Electron Spin Resonance (ESR) spectroscopy to map the quantum critical phase diagram of the heavy-fermion metal YbRh2Si2. By tracking changes in the g-factor and linewidth, the authors distinguish the physics in paramagnetic, antiferromagnetic, and quantum-critical regimes. The results offer direct, microscopic evidence supporting theories of strongly correlated electron systems near a quantum critical point.
main_problem: The study investigates how electron spin resonance (ESR) properties evolve across the quantum critical phase diagram of a heavy-fermion metal.
main_result: ESR measurements reveal distinct behaviors in the g-factor and linewidth across paramagnetic, antiferromagnetic, and quantum-critical regimes, providing microscopic insight into the underlying correlated electron physics.
method: The research combines novel, low-temperature ESR spectroscopy with theoretical modeling using effective spin Hamiltonians and molecular field approximations.
model_or_system: The system is the heavy-fermion metal YbRh2Si2, which exhibits a quantum phase transition between a paramagnetic Fermi-liquid (PFL) and an antiferromagnetic (AFL) state due to the interplay between local magnetic moments and conduction electrons.
key_observables: ESR g-factor, ESR linewidth (Delta B), and the resonance field, measured as functions of temperature and magnetic field.
important_parameters: Quantum critical point, Paramagnetic Fermi-Liquid (PFL) phase, Antiferromagnetic Liquid (AFL) phase, Kondo temperature scale ($T^*$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximating the system using an effective spin Hamiltonian and employing the molecular field approximation for theoretical modeling.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the overall phase diagram probed by ESR, show exemplary ESR spectra across different phases, and detail the temperature/field dependence of the effective g-factor, often comparing experimental fits to theoretical predictions.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model and experimental setup using ESR. It then presents results showing distinct ESR signatures in the PFL, AFL, and quantum-critical regimes, followed by theoretical analysis comparing these findings to established models of correlated electron magnetism.
why_interesting: The detailed mapping of magnetic excitations (via ESR) across a quantum critical point provides a powerful, dynamic probe of the underlying many-body interactions, which is crucial for understanding non-Fermi liquid behavior in strongly correlated materials.
